scope: Second full exact-contact rollout with reduced positional motion amplitude
summary: Reducing positional amplitude without controlling wrist orientation regresses full force closure from 296/300 to 281/300, so the change is rejected.
evidence: Nineteen frames fail force closure, beginning at source frame 315, while 281/300 pass.
Several failures have only four or five positive wrenches or positive-wrench rank below six; others retain rank six but have large origin residual.
The run still passes 298/298 causal-response frames and completes in 358.649 seconds.
lessons: Smaller Cartesian motion is not a substitute for an orientation-constrained contact mode.
A repair variable must address the diagnosed failure; amplitude tuning cannot correct unobserved wrist rotation.
limitations: Nineteen failed contact frames prevent promotion.
next_actions: Solve all seven right arm and wrist joints against a frozen grasp quaternion during contact.
